problem: Prior Habitat ObjectNav winners (SemExp, EEAux) fail mainly because of false detections from single-frame classification, poor exploration (looping, trapped, no real use of semantics), and getting trapped from imprecise depth and maps.
motivation: ObjectNav success (~24%) lags far behind PointNav (>90%). The authors analyzed failure modes and found false detection is the top cause (~48% of failures for SemExp). They also found that shuffling SemExp's semantic channels or changing its goal category costs only ~2% success, so it does not really exploit semantics for exploration.
key_idea: A simple, learning-free, semantics-agnostic corner-based exploration, combined with multi-frame verification of detections and multi-scale collision maps for trap avoidance, gives a strong modular ObjectNav baseline.
insight: Much of the gain in map-based ObjectNav comes from engineering geometry and detection robustness, not semantic exploration. Ablations show SemExp with collision avoidance is no better than Frontier exploration (GT exploration rate 58 vs 58), while Stubborn with it reaches 67. Among the collision-avoidance components, the multi-scale collision obstacle maps give the largest gain. Multi-frame verification improves the average success rate over single-frame detection (37 vs 35) but not significantly.
method: Failure analysis: manually categorize failures (false/missed detection, loop, trapped, explore, stairs, misc) for SemExp and EEAux. Ground-truth semantics and shuffled-semantics ablations show SemExp barely uses semantics for exploration.

Mapping: a 7200x7200x7 top-down map at 25cm cells. Channels are depth obstacles, pessimistic collision map (25x25cm), optimistic collision map (15x15cm), view count, summed target confidence, max target confidence and max non-target confidence. Visited path cells are always marked free.

Stubborn exploration planner: the exploration goal is one of the 4 corners of a 1200x1200 local map. The agent keeps going until the path planner finds no feasible path, then switches to the next corner clockwise. It uses no semantics and no learning.

Path planner: fast-marching method on depth OR pessimistic collision map, recomputed every step. For target goals it falls back to the optimistic map if no plan exists. Brute-force untrap mode alternates L/R turns with forward moves after 10 consecutive failed forward steps.

Two-stage target detection: RedNet (fine-tuned on 100K MP3D views) gives per-cell confidence, and a cell with score >0.5 becomes a candidate that the agent approaches. Within 1m, a per-category Naive Bayes verifier on the 4D temporal features (total views, cumulative, max, max-other confidence) decides stop or continue. It is trained on validation-trajectory data, and rejected locations are marked as false positives.
Late-episode shortcut: if the target is first found after 200 steps, verification is skipped and the agent goes straight to the target.

setting.backbone: RedNet segmentation (fine-tuned, from EEAux) + Naive Bayes verifier + rule-based exploration and fast-marching planner
setting.training_data: RedNet fine-tuned on 100K randomly sampled Matterport3D views (following EEAux); per-category Naive Bayes trained on agent trajectories on MP3D validation episodes; exploration and planning are training-free
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: move forward, turn left, turn right, stop (max 500 steps)

numbers.backbone: RedNet + Naive Bayes verifier + rule-based planner

numbers_note: The paper names the benchmark 'Habitat Object Navigation Challenge' on Matterport3D; the test SPL is printed as 0.098 (a fraction). The val numbers are for the 15 category subset. The paper's Table VI gives Habitat challenge results only for the test-standard split.
results: On the Habitat 2021 ObjectNav challenge test-standard split, Stubborn gets SR 23.7% and SPL 0.098, second on the leaderboard and well above SemExp (17.85% / 0.0707). On validation, its GT exploration rate is 67% vs 58% for Frontier and SemExp, and the trapped rate falls from 10.0% to 5.0% with all collision-avoidance components.
limitations: The multi-frame detector's improvement over single-frame (37 vs 35 average SR) is not statistically significant at 95% CI, and false detections still cause about 45% of failures.
Analyses use a small subset of categories and episodes (6 categories for SemExp, 200 episodes) and are not run under the challenge's execution-time limits.
Corner-based exploration is unsophisticated and prone to getting trapped in room corners, and it cannot use semantic priors.
